title.narrative: OUTCOME 1: Strengthened framework conditions and institutional capacity to promote climate change mitigation, adaptation and resilience through a just and inclusive green transition in the energy sector and improved meteorological services.
Policy, regulatory, procedural or capacity obstacles for enhancing a just and inclusive green energy transition and improved meteorological services have been addressed

target.value: At least one prioritised framework-related obstacle suitable for SSC intervention has been addressed in each of the 7 partner authorities as reported and evidenced in the annual report for 2027

actual.value: A planning approach based on modelling and scenarios of long term, low-cost, low carbon energy data has been adopted in Kenya and Colombia in 2024. In Brazil and Egypt the SSC provided inspiration, advise and co-analysis with the aim of having partners using improved planning tools. Globally in 2024, the SSC has contributed to the drafting of three new approved and published regulations improving VE integration in the energy sector (Kenya, Colombia). In Turkey and China focus was on integration of analysis and regulation of District Heating in the overall planning of a green energy transition. In Egypt the SSC and partners were working on a centralised register for energy efficiency in industries. In Ghana, the SSC on meteorological services has supported the foundation of a national Climate Atlas, helping the national Metrological Institute providing data and analysis to key economic sectors on climate mitigation efforts.

actual.value: Egypt and China are on track with development for an Energy Efficient Register and joint analysis on Prospects for Clean and Renewable Heating in China. Turkey is awaiting instruction

target.value: Policy, institutional and technical measures for greater renewable energy potential have been implemented [target: in two thirds of those countries where this output is planned at project level]

actual.value: In Egypt the development and integration of a centralized online platform for large consumers reporting on energy consumption and production value has started. In June 2024 the first draft version of the excel template covering the cement sector was completed. The cement sector is the first out of five sectors to be included in the online database. In Turkey, a new draft on a new heating law is inspired by the long term Danish cooperation. Standardised assessments and methods made available for local governments and energy companies are also based on the Danish approach, In China 2024 has witnessed a gradual shift in partner focus from classic heat planning towards electrification and sector coupling, as well as the regulatory and technical framework conditions needed to facilitate this. The Danish Energy Agency provides inspiration from Danish legislation and concrete cases from the Danish district heating sector, through the well established cooperation with the Chinese agencies, think tanks and universities.

title.narrative: OUTCOME 2: Enhanced Danish green diplomatic engagement in support of climate mitigation, adaptation and resilience through a just and inclusive green transition in the energy sector and improved meteorological services.

Number of Danish diplomatic outreach activities by Danish diplomatic actors that successfully use knowledge or networks supported by information arising from the FPs work on a just and inclusive green transition in the energy sector and improved meteorological services.

target.value: The programme has contributed with technical knowledge to 30 outreach actions (such as high-level meetings and policy dialogue events) which at least 4 of them, have engaged authorities and organisations beyond the SSC partner authorities, as reported and evidenced in the annual report for 2026

actual.value:
Brazil : Denmarks active participation in the G20 Energy Transitions Working Group resulted in support for the Global Coalition for Energy Planning and that the Danish Minister for Climate, Energy and Utilities, Lars Aagaard participation in the G20 Energy Ministerial Meeting in Brazil. In November, Brazil presented updated NDCs for 2035, and according to the Ministry of Environment and Climate, presentations on the Danish approach to climate planning served as inspiration for the Brazilian Climate Plan and updated NDCs. In line with the increased ambitions, Brazil accepted to become co-chair for the NDC Partnership together with Denmark.
Colombia: Denmark and Colombia are co-presidents of the Global Offshore Wind Alliance GOWA, participating in GOWA events in the UN General Assembly and COP. The purpose of GOWA is to support the large-scale deployment of offshore wind which accelerates the transition to renewable energy, strengthens international cooperation on climate action, and promotes sustainable development in the global energy sector
Kenya24 , Kenya joined the Beyond Oil and Gas Alliance (BOGA) at COP28 and was one of the first countries to get a grant from the BOGA grant facility. At COP29 in 2024, Kenya also joined the Group of Negative Emitters (GONE). The bilateral cooperation has furthermore moved from a Strategic Sector Cooperation (SSC) which ended in 2024 to a Danish Energy Partnership Programme (DEPP) starting in 2025. MOU signed on Minister-level at the first African Climate Summit in September 2023.
Egypt During Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisis first official state visit to Denmark in December 2024, the two countries entered a strategic partnership. The strategic partnership between Denmark and Egypt is one of only ten of such Danish partnerships, highlighting Egypts growing diplomatic importance to Denmark and Europe. The energy SSC played an important role in the strategic partnership agreement. The SSC MoU was extended to 2027 during a signing ceremony during the state visit with the Danish Minister of Foreign Affairs and the Egyptian Minister for Investment as signees

title.narrative: OUTPUT 1.1: Long term energy planning has improved

A comprehensive power sector model has been developed/enhanced in the partner institution and several power sector scenarios has been developed for political purposes and possibly also led to the development of Energy outlooks [target: in two thirds of those countries where this output is planned at project level]

target.value: A comprehensive power sector model has been developed/enhanced in the partner institution and several power sector scenarios has been developed for political purposes and possibly also led to the development of Energy outlooks [target: in two thirds of those countries where this output is planned at project level]

actual.value: Long term modelling and scenarios In 2024, DEA advanced long-term energy planning by supporting national institutions with modelling, data systems, and strategic planning tools that incorporated least-cost, low-carbon scenarios. In Colombia SSC supported the development of the Just Energy Transition Roadmap, a new renewable energy database, and the country's first technology catalogue, which was used by the partner for key products. In Kenya, a country specific power sector model are now used by a cross- sectoral planning unit. In Turkiye, modest progress was made on industrial demand modelling and hydrogen planning and in Brazil the SSC was supporting partners in exploring specific planning targets for installed capacity in offshore wind. The main constraints across countries continues to be lack of data or unwillingness to share sensitive energy data between institutions in the energy sector combined with low levels of cooperating on a common approach and data in planning and analysis.

Brazil. In November 2024, Brazil was one of the first countries to present its updated NDC for 2035. The NDC establishes the target of reducing Brazils net green house gas emissions to between 59pct and 57pct in 2035, compared to 2005 levels. Prior to the update, the Brazilian Ministry of Environment, responsible for developing the Brazilian Climate Plan Plano Clima was presented for the Danish approach to climate planning and an English version of the Climate Programme Executive Summary, was developed on request by the Brazilian ministry. This has served as inspiration for the Brazilian for the development of Plano Clima and the updated NDCs.
China. is currently drafting its new NDCs and the SSC seeks to support strengthened ambitions for the green transition and the climate by strengthening the partner institutions capacity for holistic energy planning and by providing input to the heating chapters of the other government to government collaboration on China Energy Transformation Outlook , CETO, which shows a costeffective pathway for carbon neutrality in Chinas energy system

target.value: Meetings held with key public, private and civil society organisations that document how information on how climate targets can be reached and extended has been shared and responded to. Target: at least 3 meetings in each of 9 countries]

actual.value:
Ghana: Ghana Meteorological Institute (GMET) chairs Ghanas National Framework for Climate Services NFCS. The NFCS was launched in 2023 and is the key policy initiative to ensure coordination of climate action efforts in Ghana. The NFCS has had a rather quiet existence so far. GMET is keen to see this change. GMET will use the analysis and data derived from the Climate Atlas to strengthen NFCSs as a platform for dialogue and coordination of climate action in Ghana.
Colombia: Denmark and Colombia are co-presidents of the Global Offshore Wind Alliance GOWA, participating in GOWA events in the UN General Assembly and COP. The purpose of GOWA is to support the large-scale deployment of offshore wind which accelerates the transition to renewable energy, strengthens international cooperation on climate action, and promotes sustainable development in the global energy sector.
Brazil: The invitation from Brazil for Denmark to join the G20 Energy Transitions Working Group resulted in a close dialogue and high level cooperation which were recognised by the Brazilian Presidency. Several high level side events with Danish participation, was held throughout the year in the margins of the G20 meetings. It culminated with the visit of the Danish Minister for Climate, Energy and Utilities to Brazil as part of the G20 Energy Ministerial Meeting. The SSC on energy was also the focus for the Danish Climate, Energy and Utilities Committee in the Danish parliament visit to Brazil. The members of the equivalent committee of Brazilian congress showed interest in the Danish approach to climate and energy issues such as hydrogen development, CBAM, offshore wind, and was followed up by technical dialog meetings with the congress members through the SSC
